title: Transforming Learning or Empty Promise? A Meta-Analysis of Generative AI in Education
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether generative AI tools in education, including ChatGPT and related large language model systems, improve student academic achievement and under what conditions they are most effective. The authors synthesize evidence from experimental and quasi-experimental studies published from late 2022 through 2025, focusing on achievement outcomes such as test scores, grades, and GPA.

The intervention studied is broad GenAI-based instructional support, including uses such as tutoring, assessment and feedback, personalized recommendation, and mixed instructional applications. The meta-analysis includes 52 independent comparisons from 54 eligible studies across K–12 and higher education, with studies spanning STEM and non-STEM fields and multiple subject areas such as language education, computer science, art, engineering, and mathematics.

Overall, GenAI-based instruction showed a large positive effect on academic achievement (Hedges' g = 1.193), though heterogeneity was very high and publication bias was detected. Moderator analyses found that instructional role and subject area significantly influenced outcomes: GenAI was most effective when used for assessment/feedback and tutoring, and language education showed the strongest gains. Educational level, sample size, learning domain, and intervention duration were not statistically significant moderators, although descriptive patterns suggested larger effects in higher education and in longer interventions. The authors conclude that GenAI can substantially support learning when it is pedagogically aligned, but that effects vary considerably by context and implementation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed meta-analysis synthesizing 52 experimental and quasi-experimental studies, which is the strongest level of evidence in the framework. It includes formal effect-size estimation, heterogeneity analysis, moderator analyses, and publication-bias testing.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effect on academic achievement is large (g = 1.193), far exceeding the blue threshold of 0.20. Although the review notes substantial heterogeneity and possible publication bias, the average impact is clearly strong and positive.

interventions.use_case: Meta-analysis of ChatGPT-like generative AI used to support learning through conversational tutoring, assessment/feedback, personalized guidance, and mixed instructional roles across K-12 and higher education.

finding.finding_summary: Across 52 independent comparisons from 54 eligible studies, GenAI-based instructional interventions produced a strong positive effect on academic achievement relative to conventional instruction. The pooled effect was Hedges' g = 1.193 (SE = 0.243, 95% CI [0.716, 1.669], p < .001), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 98.0%) indicating wide variation across contexts and implementations.
finding.measure: Academic achievement outcomes such as test scores, grades, and GPA
finding.study_size: n=52 comparisons (54 studies screened/eligible; 52 included in pooled analysis)
